<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
No existing rule ensures filenames are safe across Windows, Linux, and Mac.

The rule will apply universally. It forbids reserved names, control characters, trailing dots, and forbidden symbols on all platforms. It also blocks slashes, since that character acts as a path separator.

The rule should enforce lowercase kebab-case filenames. Leading dots should be reserved for hidden files only. Each path component must stay under 255 bytes. Percent signs should be avoided if URLs derive from filenames. NFC Unicode normalization is recommended for macOS compatibility. The rule stays general enough for any file creation workflow.

The rule will be kept under fifty lines and include actionable examples. No unrelated file changes will be made.
</details></think>

Added `.cursor/rules/safe-filenames.mdc` as an always-on rule. It applies whenever files are created, renamed, or suggested.

It covers:

- **Forbidden characters** — `/ \ : * ? " < > |`, control chars, trailing dots/spaces
- **Windows reserved names** — `CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM1`–`COM9`, `LPT1`–`LPT9`
- **Repo defaults** — lowercase kebab-case, ASCII-first, reasonable length limits
- **Normalization steps** — how to turn a user title into a safe filename
- **Rename hygiene** — grep for wikilinks, imports, and Hugo slugs when renaming
